rationale: Evidence from iteration 5 (base 1.15, mass 0.45, kp 4.2, kd 1.2, ki 0.05, 16 mm sensors at 0.025 m spacing, y 0.08, wheel_track 0.09): the oval (100% finish, 2.19 s, max_error 0.019) and s-bend (100% finish, 2.50 s, max_error 0.030) pass with margin. The slalom now fails in a different way: 20 of 20 trials time out at 0.87 progress, with zero line-loss events, max_error 0.033 and oscillation 0.35. The robot is stable on the line but too slow to cover the 4 to 5 m course in 3 s. Lowering mass from 0.5 to 0.45 (with base 1.1 to 1.15) removed every off-track ending (6 of 20 at iteration 4), so the lighter robot tracks the bends well at this speed. The remaining gap is speed. Changes: (1) base_speed 1.15 to 1.28, a moderate step that keeps the average speed high enough to finish the slalom inside 3 s; (2) all steering gains, geometry, sensors and line_loss unchanged, so the speed change can be read directly. Expected result: slalom progress rising to about 0.95 or above, with the first completions and completion_time near 2.7 to 2.9 s; oval and s-bend still finish. Risk: off-track endings return at higher speed, since iteration 3 at base 1.2 with lower kd produced 17 off-track endings on the slalom. Hypotheses: H1, if slalom off-track endings rise above about 8 of 20 with line_loss_events near 1, the bends are too fast for kp 4.2 and kd 1.2, so return to base 1.2 and raise kd to about 1.4. H2, if slalom still times out with progress near 0.9 and few off-track endings, raise base further toward 1.35 or lower mass to 0.4. H3, if oscillation on the slalom rises above about 0.6, kd is too low for this speed. Measurements wanted: slalom progress and completion_time for speed margin, slalom max_error and line_loss_events for steering margin, and steering_oscillation with control_effort for damping.
